headline: Computational recovery of finer-scale information from sparse or aggregated omics data
label: Computational Omics Analysis Tools
summary: Reference-informed and self-supervised deep or geometric models are now applied to upgrade resolution across transcriptomic, epigenomic, and nanopore data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational recovery of finer-grained information from sparse or aggregated measurements, rather than a shared modality or algorithm. In deconvolution, cellGeometry applies non-negative geometric deconvolution to estimate cell-type proportions from bulk RNA-seq using single-cell references, emphasizing speed and scale, while omnideconv provides a unifying framework that benchmarks second-generation single-cell-informed methods for accuracy, scalability, and robustness. ARUNA uses a self-supervised denoising convolutional autoencoder to impute genome-wide CpG methylation from sparse RRBS data toward WGBS resolution. Campolina applies a convolutional network to segment raw nanopore signals into events, reported to outperform Scrappie on R9.4.1 and R10.4.1 data. What is new is the extension of reference-informed and self-supervised deep or geometric models to upgrade resolution across transcriptomic, epigenomic, and nanopore data.
